items.title: System Readiness Manager User Guide
items.text:
System Readiness Manager (SRM) tracks whether Jefferson Lab's accelerators are ready to run. It holds an inventory of the machine, its systems and their components, and records each responsible group's signoff that a component has been checked and is ready. Operations and management read the result as a tree and as reports, by system, by group and by beam destination, to decide where beam can be sent. SRM is the tool behind the lab's Hot Checkout (HCO) process, and it is used all year to show the state of the machine from day to day.

At JLab, SRM is at ace.jlab.org/srm. You can view it without logging in; log in to make changes.

The guide's website has a copy for each release; pick the version the Help tab shows. On GitHub, this guide describes the main branch, which may be newer than the version you are using.

items.title: Contents
items.text:
1. Concepts: the inventory, beam destinations, responsible groups, statuses, masks and roles.
  2. Readiness: the tree that shows the state of the machine. For Operations and anyone who wants the overall picture.
  3. Signing off: checking, upgrading and downgrading components. For group members and group leaders.
  4. Masks: taking a component out of the readiness count for a while, and how masked differs from unpowered.
  5. Checklists and links: what each group verifies before it signs off, and the Links tab.
  6. Reports: status, signoff and activity reports.
  7. Administration: the Setup tab, settings and email. For admins and branch admins.
  8. FAQ: common questions about the process.
  9. Hall responsibilities: who to contact about the systems that the accelerator and the halls share.

items.title: Tabs at a glance
items.text:
Tab What it is for Readiness The machine as a tree of categories, systems, components and groups, each marked with its status. Signoff A group's signoffs for the components of one system; change them here. Masks The components that are masked now, requests to mask more, and candidates for masking. Checklists Each group's checklist for each system it is responsible for. Links Logbooks, task lists, beamline maps and sketches, and hall responsibilities. Reports Status by destination and group, signoff tables, and the history of changes. Setup Admins and branch admins only: the inventory, groups, destinations and settings. Help Version, contacts, documentation and a feedback form.

The box at the top of every page finds a component: type part of its name or alias and choose from the suggestions to open its component detail. If what you typed isn't a whole component name, SRM lists the components whose names contain it.

items.title: Quick start for group members
items.text:
1. Log in, and go to Signoff.
  2. Choose your Group, then one of its Systems, and select Apply.
  3. Read your group's checklist for the system, and check each component against it.
  4. Select the components you checked, in your group's column, and select Edit Signoff. Set the status to Checked, with a comment if there is anything to note.
  5. A group leader reviews the checked components and sets them to Ready.

When a component you signed off stops being ready, downgrade it the same way, to Checked or Not Ready, and say why in the comment. See Signing off for the details.

items.title: Quick start for Operations
items.text:
1. Go to Readiness, select Choose... and pick the Beam Destination you want to send beam to, or Current Run for all of the run's destinations.
  2. A green thumbs-up at the top of the tree means every component for that destination is Ready or masked. Otherwise open the nodes that aren't Ready to find the components and the groups that are holding it back.
  3. Check Masks › Current for what is masked and until when.

items.title: Questions and changes
items.text: Use the feedback form on the Help tab, or contact the content and technical contacts listed there. To suggest a change to this guide, open an issue or pull request on GitHub.

items.title: Administration
items.text:
User Guide › Administration

The Setup tab is where the inventory, the groups and the settings are maintained. It is shown to admins and branch admins only.

items.title: Who can do what
items.text:
• An admin has the srm-admin role and can do everything in SRM.
  • A branch admin administers one branch: a top-level category, such as a hall, with everything below it. A branch's admins are the users with the branch's Admin Role, which an admin sets on the Category Tree. Any role of the user directory can be used, so a new branch needs no change to SRM.
  • A group leader is a member of the role named as the group's Leader Workgroup on the Group List.
  • A crew chief has the cc role.

Roles are managed in the lab's user directory, not in SRM. A change to who is an admin or a branch admin takes effect the next time the person logs in. A change to who leads a group takes effect when SRM's copy of the directory is refreshed: every night, or at once with Clear on the Directory Cache page.

Branch admins see the whole inventory on the Setup pages, and SRM refuses with "Not authorized" when they try to change something outside their branch. The pages they can use are Category Tree, Component List, Component Part., System Part., Group Resp. and Bulk Signoff; the rest are for admins.

Every change to a category, system or component is recorded, with who made it and when, in the Inventory Activity report.

items.title: Category Tree
items.text:
Setup › Category Tree shows the categories and systems, and adds, edits and removes them. Components are on the Component List.

Under Category and System, Add..., Edit... and Remove... open a dialog. For Edit and Remove, first choose the category or system; for Add and Edit, fill in:

Field Meaning Parent The category it goes under. A category can also go at the top level, which makes it a branch; only an admin can do that. Name Unique among all categories, or among all systems. Weight A whole number that orders it among its siblings: lower first; blank last, by name. Admin Role Top-level categories only, and admins only: the role whose members are the branch's admins. Description Systems only. Shown in the System Information dialog.

Removing a system removes its components and its group responsibilities with it, and removing a category removes its systems the same way, so SRM asks you to confirm. An admin can rename the top of the tree with Root....

items.title: Component List
items.text:
Setup › Component List adds and maintains components. Use the filter to find them, by Beam Destination, Category, System, Region, Group, Source, Masked, Unpowered or Component name (with % as a wildcard). The list can include components of systems that don't take part in Readiness; see System participation.

Button Does Add Adds a component: its Name, System and Region. Each of the system's responsible groups gets a Not Ready signoff for it. Bulk Add Adds several components to one system and region, one name to a line. If any name is refused, none are added. Rename Changes the name. The signoffs and their history stay with the component. Remove Deletes the component with its signoffs. It no longer appears in the reports, including the activity reports. (Un)mask Sets or removes a Masked (Administrator) mask, with a reason and an expiration. Removing the mask sets the component's signoffs to Not Ready, as the dialog warns, with the Masked Reason, if any, as the comment. See Masks. (Un)power Marks the component unpowered, or powered again. Changing it sets the component's signoffs to Not Ready. Edit System Moves the component to another system. Groups responsible for both systems keep their signoffs; the others' signoffs are deleted, and groups new to the component start at Not Ready. Edit Region Changes the region. Edit Source Says where the component's record comes from: INTERNAL, or an element database (CED, LED, UED) with the element's ID there. The component's detail then links to that element. Edit Alias Sets another name the component is known by. The search box finds it, and the component's detail shows it.

A name can't contain an asterisk, and must be unique within its system. For a component whose source is an element database, SRM warns before a rename or a move, since the name and system should follow the database.

items.title: Component participation
items.text:
Setup › Component Part. sets which beam destinations each component takes part in. It is a grid of components (rows) by destinations (columns), where a ✔ means the component is needed to send beam there.

Select a cell to switch it; it is saved at once. The grid shows five destinations and ten components at a time: use the filters to choose the components and the destination columns, the Previous and Next links to move through them, and 10 | 100 | 1000 to show more rows.

A component that takes part in no destination only shows on the other pages when their Beam Destination filter is empty.

items.title: System participation
items.text:
Setup › System Part. sets which applications each system takes part in. SRM's inventory of systems and components is shared with other applications, such as Downtime and Problem Report, and a ✔ under Readiness is what makes a system part of SRM's readiness and signoffs. Select a cell to switch it.

A system without the Readiness ✔, and its components, doesn't appear on the Readiness or Signoff tabs or in the reports.

items.title: Group responsibilities
items.text:
Setup › Group Resp. sets, for one system, the ordered list of groups that sign off its components. Choose the system first.

  • Add a group and say whether a Checklist Required. The group goes at the end of the order, and every component of the system gets a Not Ready signoff for it.
  • Edit changes Checklist Required. When it is Yes, the group can't sign off the system until its checklist is published.
  • Remove deletes the group's signoffs for the system's components. Their history stays in the activity reports.
  • Drag a row by its handle to change the Order; it is saved at once. Existing signoffs don't change. The order decides whose turn it is and which groups a downgrade cascades to.

items.title: Bulk Signoff
items.text:
Setup › Bulk Signoff sets every signoff of one or more systems, for every responsible group and every component that isn't masked, to the same status with the same comment. It is for starting or resetting a checkout, for example setting a whole system to Not Ready at the start of a maintenance period.

Choose the System or systems, the Status (Ready, Checked or Not Ready) and a Comment, and select Signoff. SRM works through the systems one at a time and shows each as Queued, Working, Done or Failed.

Bulk signoff skips the usual signoff rules: a signoff can go straight from Not Ready to Ready, required checklists aren't checked, and downgrades don't cascade. Setting Ready still needs an admin, a leader of each group, or an admin of the system's branch. There is no undo, short of another bulk signoff.

items.title: Region List, Group List, Beam Destination List and Status List
items.text: These are for admins.

items.title: Region List
items.text: The regions in order, with their aliases. The list is read-only: regions are added and changed in the database.

items.title: Group List
items.text:
The responsible groups, including archived ones. Add or Edit a group's:

Field Meaning Name Unique. Description Shown in the Group Information dialog. Leader Workgroup The role in the user directory whose members are the group's leaders. Archived Hides the group from the lists where a group is chosen, such as the Signoff tab and the Checklists tab.

A group can't be removed here; archive it instead.

items.title: Beam Destination List
items.text:
The beam destinations in order, with a Target checkbox for each. The targets are the Current Run destinations: what most pages start with, and what the Current Run link beside a Beam Destination filter chooses. Tick or untick a checkbox to change them, at the start of each run; it is saved at once. The Facility filter shows one facility's destinations, and No Target clears the targets shown.

Destinations themselves are added and changed in the database.

items.title: Status List
items.text: The statuses, in order from best to worst. Read-only.

items.title: Saved Signoffs
items.text:
Setup › Saved Signoffs, for admins, keeps signoffs that are made again and again, so they can be repeated with a few clicks. The main use is the forced re-check at the end of a run: downgrading each group's Ready signoffs to Checked, system by system, so that the groups look at their components again.

A saved signoff is a filter, as on the Signoff tab, with the status and comment to apply:

Field Meaning Signoff Type A label for grouping them: CEBAF or LERF. With Autofill name and comments, the name and comment are made from the group, system and type. Signoff Name Unique. Status, Comments What to set. With Downgrade Only, the choices are Checked and Not Ready. Group, System Whose signoffs, on which system. Region, Status, Component Name Optional: only the components in a region, only the signoffs with a given status now, or only the names that match.

To make one, select Add; or set up the filter on the Signoff tab and select Save Named Signoff there. A saved signoff can't be edited: remove it and add it again.

To use them:

  • Select one or more rows and select Signoff to make them all at once. The normal signoff rules apply, and a downgrade cascades: later groups' Ready signoffs become Checked. Select at most one saved signoff per system: since a downgrade cascades, two on one system can change the same signoffs, so SRM refuses the whole selection and names the systems selected more than once.
  • Or select the 🔗 button on a row to open the Signoff tab with that saved signoff's filter, status and comment filled in, to review the components before saving.

Both ways apply the Max Last Modified Date set on this page: signoffs changed after it are left alone. Set it to the start of the maintenance period, so that signoffs made since then aren't downgraded.

To downgrade Ready signoffs to Checked without upgrading the ones that are Not Ready, set the filter's Status to Ready; Downgrade Only does that for you.

items.title: Email
items.text:
SRM sends three kinds of email:

Email Sent To Mask request When someone requests a mask. The addresses in the EMAIL_MASK_REQUEST_LIST setting. Activity report Daily at 7:00, when EMAIL_ACTIVITY_ENABLED is on. The addresses in the EMAIL_ACTIVITY_LIST setting. Group action report Daily at 7:00, when EMAIL_LEADERS_ENABLED is on. The leaders of each group.

The two daily reports cover the day before, from 7:00 to 7:00. The activity report lists the signoff changes that left a component Checked or Not Ready: the new outstanding work. The group report lists the same for one group, such as a downgrade of that group's signoff or a cascade to it, each with a link to the Signoff tab for that group and system. The group report lists only the components in the Current Run destinations, so a group isn't emailed about destinations that aren't running; with no Current Run destination, it lists nothing. A report with nothing in it isn't sent.

Feedback from the Help tab's form is emailed to the admins.

Setup › Email, for admins, shows who receives each email, shows whether the daily emails are on, and has a Preview of each report. Send Now sends a report at once, and Send To All sends every group its report. The recipients and the on/off switches are settings.

items.title: Settings and Directory Cache
items.text:
Setup › Settings lists the settings, by tag, and an admin can Edit a value. A change takes effect at once unless the setting's description says the app must be redeployed.

Setting Meaning EMAIL_MASK_REQUEST_LIST Who is emailed about mask requests: addresses, separated by commas. EMAIL_ACTIVITY_ENABLED, EMAIL_ACTIVITY_LIST Whether the daily activity report is sent, and to whom. EMAIL_LEADERS_ENABLED Whether the daily group action reports are sent to group leaders. EMAIL_ENABLED, EMAIL_TESTING_ENABLED, EMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS For the Help tab's feedback form: whether it sends email, whether it sends to the test group instead of the admins, and the sender's address. HELP_CONTENT_CONTACT, HELP_TECHNICAL_CONTACT, HELP_DOC_CSV The contacts and the documentation links on the Help tab. Each documentation link is URL\|Label. LINKS_GENERAL_CSV, LINKS_SKETCH_CSV The links in the General and Beamline Sketches sections of the Links tab, in order, separated by commas: each is URL\|Label, and a label cannot contain a comma. A URL can start with {CED_SERVER_URL}, which stands for the CEBAF Element Database's address. Only http, https and relative URLs are shown, and a section with no links is hidden. NOTIFICATION_ENABLED, NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE, NOTIFICATION_LINK_NAME, NOTIFICATION_LINK_URL A banner across the top of every page, such as a notice of maintenance, with an optional link. IP_READ_FILTER_ENABLED, IP_READ_ALLOWLIST_PATTERN, IP_READ_URL_PATTERN Whether viewing without a login is limited to some network addresses, and which. ADMIN_ROLE_NAME The role that can edit settings, is listed on the Help tab and receives feedback. SMOOTHNESS_CDN_ENABLED, SMOOTHNESS_SERVER Where shared page resources are served from.

Values changed directly in the database take effect after Refresh Cache.

Setup › Directory Cache shows the users and roles SRM has looked up in the user directory, which it keeps until midnight. Select Clear after someone is added to or removed from a group's leaders, so that it takes effect without waiting for the night.

Server settings, such as the logbook server and which logbooks receive problem reports, are environment variables; see the README.

items.title: Help tab
items.text: The Help tab shows the release version and date, the content and technical contacts, the admins (when you are logged in), links to documentation, including this guide, and a feedback form that emails the admins.

items.title: Checklists and links
items.text: User Guide › Checklists and links

items.title: Checklists
items.text:
A checklist says what a group actually verifies before it signs off the components of a system. There is one for each pairing of a responsible group and a system, so two groups that sign off the same system each have their own. Publishing the checklists means that anyone, from the next group in line to the Crew Chief, can see what a Ready from that group stands for.

Anyone can read the checklists and their history without logging in.

items.title: Finding a checklist
items.text:
On the Checklists tab, choose a group. The page lists the systems the group is responsible for:

Column Meaning System The system the checklist is for. Checklist Required Whether the group must publish a checklist before it can sign off this system. An admin sets this on Setup › Group Resp. Published Whether it is published, and by whom and when. Checklist View, History and, depending on who you are, Create, Edit, Delete and Sign & Publish or Unpublish.

View opens the checklist with its document ID, group, system, author, revision number, date and comment. Printer Friendly opens it as a page of its own for printing. Published checklists are also linked from the Group Information, System Information and Component Information dialogs elsewhere in SRM.

items.title: Writing a checklist
items.text:
1. Log in, choose your group on the Checklists tab, and select Create beside the system (or Edit if there is one already).
  2. Fill in the Author: the person who is responsible for the content, who needn't be the person typing.
  3. Write the checklist in the editor. Bulleted list items are shown with a checkbox, so write each check as a bullet. The Insert template button offers two outlines, Uncredited Control Level 1 and Uncredited Control Level 2, with headings for system validation and for the system's performance specification documents.
  4. When editing, give a Revision Comment saying what changed.
  5. Select Save.

The editor keeps text formatting, headings, lists and links. It doesn't keep images or tables.

Every save is kept as a revision. History lists them, oldest first, with the revision number, date, comment, author and who submitted it; View shows the checklist as it was. An old revision can't be restored, but its text can be copied into a new one.

items.title: Publishing
items.text:
A group leader or an admin publishes a checklist with Sign & Publish, which records their name and the date, and can Unpublish or Delete it. Deleting removes the checklist with all of its history.

Not published Published Create, Edit Any logged-in user A leader of the group, or an admin Sign & Publish, Unpublish, Delete A leader of the group, or an admin A leader of the group, or an admin

Editing a published checklist leaves it published, with the new revision showing at once.

items.title: Required checklists
items.text: Where Checklist Required is Yes and the checklist isn't published, the group can't sign off that system: the Signoff tab says that a checklist "must be published before signoffs can be made" and lists no components. Admins are exempt. To see which checklists are still missing, use the Group Responsibility report.

items.title: Links
items.text:
The Links tab collects references that are useful during a checkout:

  • General: the logbooks, the task lists, the beamline map, the songsheets, the hall and beam dump responsibility documents, and the Accelerator Bypassed-Interlocks Log (on site only).
  • Beamline Sketches: the CEBAF Element Database's sketch of each part of the machine, from the injector to the halls and the LERF.

Admins change the links in the LINKS_GENERAL_CSV and LINKS_SKETCH_CSV settings, on the Setup tab, and the tab shows them at once.

items.title: Concepts
items.text: User Guide › Concepts

items.title: Why track readiness
items.text:
An accelerator is made of thousands of components, looked after by dozens of groups. Before beam is sent somewhere after a maintenance period, each group has to confirm that its part of every device on the way is back in working order: this is the lab's Hot Checkout (HCO). System Readiness Manager (SRM) is where that is recorded. It answers two questions:

  • For Operations and management: is the machine ready to send beam to this destination, and if not, what is left and who has it?
  • For each group: which components are waiting on us?

SRM is used all year, not only during a hot checkout. When a component breaks or is worked on during a run, its group downgrades it, so SRM keeps showing the state of the machine.

items.title: Categories, systems and components
items.text:
The inventory is a tree:

  • A component is one thing to be checked: a magnet, a beam position monitor, a valve, a server, a procedure.
  • A system is a set of components of the same kind, such as "Box Power Supplies" or "Beam Valves". The components of a system share the same checklist and the same responsible groups, which is what makes them a system.
  • A category groups systems, and other categories, for reporting: for example CEBAF › Magnets › Box Supply. The top-level categories, such as CEBAF, LERF and each hall, are branches, and a branch can have its own admins.

A component also has:

  • a region: where it is in the machine; see Regions;
  • the beam destinations it takes part in; see Beam destinations;
  • optionally an alias, another name it is known by, which the search box also finds;
  • a source: INTERNAL when it was entered in SRM, or the element database it comes from (CED for CEBAF, LED for the LERF, UED for the UITF), with a link to the element there.

A component's name is unique within its system.

items.title: Beam destinations
items.text:
A beam destination is somewhere beam can be sent: a hall, a dump, a Faraday cup, a tune-up line. Each component is marked with the destinations it takes part in, which is every destination that needs it to be working. An injector magnet takes part in nearly all of them; a magnet in a hall's transport line only in that hall's.

Filtering by beam destination, on the Readiness tab and in nearly every report, turns "is the machine ready?" into the question Operations actually asks: "is everything ready that we need to send beam there?"

The Current Run link beside a Beam Destination filter chooses the destinations of the current run, and most pages start with them chosen. An admin sets which destinations those are on Setup › Beam Dest. List.

items.title: Regions
items.text: A region is a stretch of the machine, such as the Injector, the North Linac, an arc or a hall's beam line. Every component is in one region. Regions are a second way to cut the inventory: a system such as "Beam Valves" runs through the whole machine, and the region picks out its components in one place.

items.title: Responsible groups
items.text:
A responsible group is a team that checks components: Alignment, Vacuum, DC Power, RF, Safety Systems, Operations and so on. Each system has an ordered list of the groups responsible for it, and every component of the system needs a signoff from each of them.

The order is the order the work is done in, each group building on the one before: for example the group that installs a device, then the group that powers it, then the group that controls it. It matters in two ways: SRM shows each group the components where it is its turn, and a downgrade by one group can cascade to the groups after it.

Each group has leaders, who make the final Ready signoff. A group can also have a checklist for each system, saying what its signoff means.

items.title: Statuses
items.text:
A signoff is one group's status for one component:

Status Meaning Who sets it Not Ready Not checked yet, or known not to work. Every signoff starts here. Any logged-in user. Checked A member of the group has checked the component, and it is waiting for the leader's review. Any logged-in user. Ready The group stands behind the component for beam operations. A leader of the group, an admin or a branch admin. Not Applicable This group has nothing to check on this component, though it does on others in the system. A leader of the group, an admin or a branch admin.

Signing off is a two-step process: a technician or engineer checks the component and marks it Checked, then a group leader reviews and marks it Ready. See Signoff rules.

A component's status is the worst of its groups' signoffs, in the order Not Ready, Checked, Ready; Not Applicable signoffs are passed over. A component is Ready only when every responsible group has signed it off as Ready or Not Applicable. A masked component shows its mask instead.

A system's status is the worst of its components', and a category's the worst of its systems', leaving masked components out. On the Readiness tab these follow the filter, so the same category can be Ready for one beam destination and Not Ready for another.

items.title: Masks
items.text: A mask takes a component out of the count for a while: it is broken or out of service, a repair is planned, and the program can run without it. A masked component no longer holds back its system. A mask has a reason and, normally, an expiration; when it ends, the component's groups have to sign it off again. There are three kinds, Masked (Director), Masked (Crew Chief) and Masked (Administrator), named for how the mask was made. See Masks.

items.title: Unpowered components
items.text: An unpowered component, marked with a ★ after its name, is one that isn't meant to be used during the run. It still has to be signed off: the groups verify that it can't affect the beam. Changing a component between powered and unpowered sets its signoffs back to Not Ready, since what has to be verified changes. See Unpowered or masked?

items.title: Roles
items.text:
Anyone can view SRM without logging in. What you can change depends on who you are:

Role Who Can Logged-in user Anyone with a lab account. Sign off components as Checked or Not Ready, comment, request a mask, and write a checklist that isn't published yet. Group leader A leader or supervisor of a responsible group. Also sign off as Ready or Not Applicable for the group, and edit, publish and delete the group's checklists. Receives the group's daily email. Crew Chief The Operations crew chiefs. Also mask components directly, and edit and remove masks. Branch admin The admins of one top-level category, such as a hall. Also set up their branch on the Setup tab (categories, systems, components, responsibilities), and sign off as Ready or Not Applicable for any group on their branch's components. Admin The SRM administrators, listed on the Help tab. Everything, including accepting mask requests, the lists of groups and destinations, saved signoffs, and settings.

Group leaders, crew chiefs and admins are roles in the lab's user directory; see Administration for how each is set.

The process also has people whose part is to read SRM, not to change it:

  • Geographic integrators: the liaison for an area of the machine, who works with the groups to get the area ready. The Region filter gives their view.
  • Management: the Program Deputy, Operability and the Operations department follow the progress, including at the daily meetings, through the reports.
  • Operations: decides where beam can be sent from the readiness of each beam destination.

items.title: Frequently asked questions
items.text:
User Guide › FAQ

SRM was first called the Hot Checkout (HCO) tool, and many people still call it HCO; the two names mean the same application.

items.title: When should I downgrade a component?
items.text: Whenever you work on a component and you are not its final signoff, so that the groups after yours are told to look again, and whenever a component won't be operational for more than a shift. The link in ATLis takes you straight to the component's signoff in SRM. Always write a comment when you downgrade, and upgrade the component again once it is back in service. Operations relies on this to understand the state of the machine from day to day. See Downgrades and cascades.

items.title: Can the accelerator operate when not everything is ready?
items.text: Yes. The accelerator is a large machine that will rarely, if ever, have every component working. At the start of a run the aim is for SRM to be completely ready ("all green"), with the components that are known to be out of service masked. Once the run starts, components break and need repair, which is coordinated through the Ops PR process. If a repair can't be made during the shift, downgrade the component so that the Crew Chief knows the state of the machine. The program changes during a run too, so some components will be not ready or waiting for a scheduled repair; what matters is that the Crew Chief can review SRM and see the actual state of each system.

items.title: What if SRM says my group is responsible for a component we don't work on?
items.text: The signoffs were negotiated with system owners and group leaders when the Hot Checkout process was designed, by system: every component of a system has the same groups. If your group works on some of a system's components and not others, a group leader can sign off the others as Not Applicable. SRM makes sure at least one group checks every component, so the last group left can't choose Not Applicable. If you think the assignment itself is wrong, use the feedback form on the Help tab.

items.title: What does a Not Applicable (N/A) signoff mean?
items.text:
• It belongs to one group on one component: one group can be N/A while another still signs off.
  • It is for a component a group never checks, in a system where the group normally does sign off.
  • It doesn't expire. It stays until someone sets the signoff to Not Ready, Checked or Ready again.
  • It exists only in SRM; the CEBAF Element Database (CED) doesn't set or read it.

For example, most CEBAF box power supplies are interlocked by the Personnel Safety System, so the Safety Systems Group signs off the Box Power Supplies system. A few of them aren't interlocked, and for those the group's signoff is N/A.

items.title: How do I sign off an unpowered component? What about masking?
items.text: An unpowered component still needs its signoffs; a masked component doesn't. See Unpowered or masked?

items.title: When does Hot Checkout happen?
items.text:
SRM is used all year, and Hot Checkout is the part of the year when the machine goes from a maintenance period back to running. It typically has two stages:

  1. Before tunnel lockup: the checks that make the machine ready to lock up, such as alignment, vacuum work and diagnostic health checks. These are done during the maintenance period, up to the week before lockup.
  2. After tunnel lockup: the checks that need the tunnel locked, such as box power supply and RF checks. These are done in the week before beam operations, starting on Monday, with the turnover to Operations complete by Friday morning.

At the end of a run, a chosen set of components is downgraded on purpose so that the responsible groups check them again; see Saved Signoffs.

items.title: Who do I ask about SRM, or to get something changed?
items.text: Use the feedback form on the Help tab. The message goes to the whole team, so questions are answered and concerns are followed up. To suggest a change to this guide, open an issue or pull request on GitHub.

items.title: Hall responsibilities
items.text:
User Guide › Hall responsibilities

Who to contact about the beamline systems that the accelerator and the experimental halls share. The responsible groups that sign off each system in SRM are on the Group Responsibility report; the Links tab has the responsibility documents for the other halls and the beam dumps.

items.title: Masks
items.text:
User Guide › Masks

A mask takes a component out of the readiness count for a while. Use it for a component that is broken or out of service and waiting for repair, when the program can run without it. A masked component shows a mask instead of a status, and it no longer holds back its system, its category or its beam destinations: the Readiness tree and the reports count it separately.

A mask has a reason, the person who set it, and normally an expiration: the date by which the component will be dealt with, or the end of the run, whichever comes first. Components that are credited controls, or that the run can't do without, are never masked.

Anyone can view the Masks tab without logging in.

items.title: Kinds of mask
items.text:
The kind records how the mask was made, and is shown as the component's status:

Kind How it is made Who can make it Masked (Director) An admin accepts a mask request. Any logged-in user can ask; an admin accepts. Masked (Crew Chief) Mask on Candidates. A crew chief or an admin. Masked (Administrator) (Un)mask on Setup › Component List. An admin, or a branch admin in their branch.

Whichever way a component is masked, each of its group signoffs is set to the mask too, with the comment "Masked", so the signoff history shows when it happened.

items.title: Requesting a mask
items.text:
1. On the Signoff tab, list the system's components and select the ones to mask, in your group's column.
  2. Select Request Masking.
  3. Give the Reason (up to 512 characters) and the Mask Expiration, which must be in the future.
  4. Select Save.

SRM creates one request for each component, emails the people who handle mask requests, and shows the pending requests. It refuses a component that is already masked or already has a pending request; nothing is requested if any of the selected components is refused.

items.title: Requests
items.text:
Masks › Requests lists the requests, newest first: the response (PENDING, ACCEPTED or REJECTED), component, system, reason, mask expiration, who asked and when. It starts with the pending requests for the current run's destinations; the filter can show the others, by Beam Destination, Category, System, Region, Group, Reason and Request Status. Export saves the list as an image or prints it.

An admin selects a request and then:

  • Accept: the dialog shows the reason and expiration that were asked for, and either can be changed before saving. The component gets a Director mask, with the admin as the person who masked it.
  • Reject: the request is marked REJECTED and nothing else changes. The component can be requested again.

SRM doesn't email the requester about the answer, so look at the request on this page, or tell them.

items.title: Current masks
items.text:
Masks › Current lists the components that are masked now, the most recently masked first: the masked date, the mask expiration date, the component and its system, who masked it and the kind of mask, and the reason. Select a component's name for its Component Information.

The filter starts with the current run's destinations and with the Director and Crew Chief masks. To see Administrator masks, add Administrator to Mask Type. It can also filter by Category, System, Region, Group, Unpowered and Component name (with % as a wildcard).

A crew chief or an admin can select one or more rows (hold Ctrl or Shift, ⌘ on a Mac) and then:

  • Edit Mask: change the reason and expiration. The dialog starts with the first selected component's reason and expiration, and warns when the other selected components' differ: saving gives every selected component the dialog's values. The reason is required: to unmask, use Remove Mask. Clear the expiration for a mask that doesn't expire. The mask keeps its kind, its masked date and who masked it; the signoff history records the edit as "Mask edited", with you and the time.
  • Remove Mask: unmask the components. Choose the Status their signoffs go to, Checked (the default) or Not Ready, and optionally a Comment for the signoff history.

items.title: Candidates
items.text:
Masks › Candidates lists the components that aren't masked and aren't Ready: by default those that are Checked or Not Ready, for the current run's destinations. It is the list to work through when deciding what the run can start without. The filter can change the Status and narrow the list by Beam Destination, Category, System, Region, Group, Unpowered and Component name.

A crew chief or an admin can select components and select Mask, giving the Reason, which is required, and the Expiration. This makes a Crew Chief mask at once, with no request.

items.title: When a mask ends
items.text:
How it ends The component's signoffs become The expiration passes Not Ready, with the comment "Auto-downgrade due to unmasking by expiration". Remove Mask on Masks › Current Checked or Not Ready, as chosen. (Un)mask on Setup › Component List Not Ready, with the Masked Reason as the comment, or "Auto-downgrade due to unmasking" if it is empty.

Either way, every responsible group then has to look at the component again and sign off. Expired masks are removed at midnight, and whenever someone opens the Readiness tab, so a mask can outlast its expiration time by up to a day in the other pages. A mask with no expiration stays until someone removes it.

While a component is masked, by any kind of mask, its signoffs can't be changed: remove the mask first.

items.title: Unpowered or masked?
items.text:
These are different things, and a component can be both.

Unpowered means the component isn't meant to be used during the run. It follows the element's property in the CEBAF Element Database (CED); an admin sets it in SRM with (Un)power on Setup › Component List, and SRM marks the component with a ★.

  • Unpowered elements don't appear on the control screens.
  • The groups still sign off an unpowered component as Not Ready, Checked or Ready. Checking an unpowered component is a hot checkout in reverse: verify that it can't affect the beam in any way.

Masked means the component is broken or out of service, with a repair planned. It exists only in SRM; CED doesn't set or read it.

  • A mask should have an expiration: the date by which the component will be dealt with, or the end of the run, whichever comes first.
  • While it is masked, all of its group signoffs are masked.
  • Credited controls, show-stoppers and critical components are never masked.

Which to use:

The component Use works after a standard checkout, but won't be used this run and has had its controls removed Unpowered, not masked. is broken or out of service, with a repair planned, and should stay on the control screens Masked. is broken or out of service, with a repair planned, and shouldn't show on the control screens Unpowered and masked.

Vacuum elements are never hidden from the control screens, whether or not their controls have been removed, so they aren't marked unpowered.

items.title: Readiness
items.text:
User Guide › Readiness

The Readiness tab is the front page of SRM: the whole machine as a tree, each node colored by its status. Operations uses it to see whether beam can be sent to a destination and, if not, which components and groups are holding it back. Anyone can view it without logging in.

items.title: The tree
items.text:
The tree follows the inventory: categories contain categories or systems, systems contain components, and each component lists its responsible groups in signoff order.

Node Its status Group (under a component) That group's signoff for the component. A group that hasn't signed off yet is Not Ready. Component The worst of its groups' signoffs, or its mask if it is masked. System The worst of its components that match the filter, leaving out masked components. Category The worst of the systems below it.

A system or category with nothing to check (no components match, or all of them are masked) shows Ready. The Status Key and Node Key beside the tree explain the icons: a green thumbs-up is Ready, a yellow check mark is Checked, and a red cross is Not Ready. A ★ after a component's name marks it as unpowered.

Open a node to see what is below it. Expand All opens every category and system at once, and is only available when the filter leaves 100 components or fewer; with that few, the tree opens by itself. Collapse All closes everything. The tree remembers which nodes you had open.

Select a component to open its Component Information dialog, the same page as the component detail report.

items.title: Filtering
items.text:
Choose... opens the filter. The line under the page title says what is selected and, in braces, how many components match; Clear removes the filter.

Filter Keeps components Beam Destination (Include) that take part in any of the chosen beam destinations. The Current Run link chooses the destinations of the current run. Category, System in that part of the inventory. Choosing a category narrows the System list. Region in that region of the machine. Group that the group is responsible for. Status whose status is one of the chosen ones. Beam Destination (Exclude) that take part in none of the chosen destinations.

The statuses of systems and categories follow the filter. For example, with Beam Destination set to one hall, a category is Ready when every component needed for that hall is Ready, whatever the state of the rest of the machine.

When masked components match the filter, the selection line ends with a link such as (3 Masked), which opens the current masks with the same filter.

items.title: Recent Activity
items.text: The Recent Activity panel lists the five latest signoff changes that match the filter: when, who, the kind of change, the system and component (and how many more components were signed off with it), the comment, and the group and its new status. Components signed off together are one entry. Show more adds the next ten entries, and Signoff Activity opens the Signoff Activity report with the same filter, which has a row for each component.

items.title: Signing off from the tree
items.text: Select a group under a component to change that one signoff; SRM asks you to log in first. The Edit Group Signoff dialog has the same Status, Comment and Needs Attention fields as the Signoff tab, and the same rules apply, with one difference: a downgrade made here doesn't cascade to the groups after yours. To sign off several components at once, or to downgrade with a cascade, use the Signoff tab.

items.title: Export
items.text: Export › System Excel downloads a spreadsheet of the whole inventory outline: every category and system, indented as in the tree, with the number of components in each system. It ignores the filter.

items.title: Reports
items.text:
User Guide › Reports

The Reports tab has ten reports, listed in the menu on the left. Anyone can read them without logging in, except Inventory Activity, which is for admins and branch admins.

Report Answers Overall Status How much of the machine is signed off? Group Status How far along is each group? Signoff Summary How many signoffs changed in a period, and which way? Signoff What is the state of each group's signoff on each component? Component Which components have a given status, and what is known about one component? Group Responsibility Which groups sign off which systems, and are their checklists published? Group Leader Who leads each group? Signoff Activity Who changed which signoff, when and why? Inventory Activity Who changed the inventory? All Activity What happened, signoffs and inventory together?

items.title: Using the reports
items.text:
Choose... opens a report's filter, and Apply runs it. Clear empties the filter; where there is a Reset, it goes back to the report's starting filter. The line under the title says what is selected and, in braces, how many rows match. Lists show 100 rows a page.

  • Beam Destination keeps the components that take part in any of the chosen destinations. Most reports start with the current run's destinations chosen; the Current Run link chooses them again. Some reports can also Exclude destinations: that leaves out the components that take part in any of those.
  • Category covers the systems in the category and in the categories below it, and narrows the System list.
  • Component matches a whole name unless you use % as a wildcard: MQB% finds the names that start with MQB, and %2L% those that contain 2L.
  • Date Range offers periods such as Today (from 7:00), Past 7 Days, Current CC Shift and Previous Month; Custom... takes a start (included) and an end (not included). Days start at 7:00.

A report's address includes its filter, so a report can be bookmarked or sent to someone as it is. SRM also remembers the last filter you used on each report while your browser session lasts.

Where a report has them, Full Screen shows the report alone, for a wall display or a meeting, and Export offers Image (a picture of the report) and Print.

How the reports count:

  • A signoff is one group's status for one component. A component with three responsible groups has three signoffs, so the status reports count signoffs, not components.
  • A signoff that was never made is Not Ready.
  • The status charts leave out masked components and Not Applicable signoffs.
  • Unpowered components count like any others.

items.title: Overall Status
items.text: A pie chart of the signoffs that are Ready, Checked and Not Ready, with the count and percentage of each and the total. This is the progress of a hot checkout at a glance: filter it by Beam Destination, Category, System, Region or Group to see the progress toward one destination or of one part of the machine.

items.title: Group Status
items.text:
The same counts for each responsible group: the group's total signoffs, how many are Ready, Checked and Not Ready, and each as a percentage, with a small pie chart. Under Display, choose Bar to see the groups as stacked bars instead of a table.

Select a count to open the Signoff report with those signoffs listed.

items.title: Signoff Summary
items.text:
How many signoffs changed during a period, starting with yesterday 7:00 to today 7:00. Change Count has a row for each kind of change, and Change Count By Group has the same counts for each group that had any:

Change Meaning Upgrade Ready Signed off as Ready. Upgrade Checked Raised from Not Ready to Checked. Downgrade Checked Lowered from Ready to Checked. Downgrade Not Ready Lowered to Not Ready. Cascade Lowered to Checked because an earlier group downgraded; see cascades. Comment A comment added without changing the status.

Select a count to open Signoff Activity with those changes listed.

items.title: Signoff
items.text:
The current state of every signoff: Component, Group, Modified Date, Modified By, Status and Comments, 100 to a page. Beyond the common filters it has:

  • Status: one or more of Not Applicable, Ready, Checked and Not Ready.
  • Ready Turn: Yes lists the signoffs that are waiting on their own group, because the groups before it are done; see Whose turn it is.
  • Masked: Yes or No to list only the signoffs of masked or unmasked components.

From a row, the component's name opens its Component Information, the status opens the Signoff tab at that component and group, and the comment icon opens the signoff's history.

Export › Excel downloads every row that matches the filter, not just the page shown.

items.title: Component
items.text:
Lists components with their System, Region and overall Status. A component's status is the worst of its groups' signoffs, or its mask; see Statuses. Filter by Status to list, for example, everything that is Not Ready for a destination, or by Unpowered to list the unpowered components.

From a row, the name opens the Component Information dialog, the status opens the Signoff tab at that component, and the → button opens the component's own page.

items.title: Component detail
items.text:
The Component Information dialog, and the page with the same content, shows what SRM knows about one component. It opens from a component's name almost anywhere in SRM and from the search box at the top of every page.

Field Shows Alias Another name the component is known by, if it has one. Group Signoff Each responsible group in signoff order, with its status, when and by whom it was last changed, and the comment. Signoff goes to the Signoff tab for that group; Activity shows that signoff's history. Group Responsibilities The groups again, each with its Group Information and, when published, its checklist. Category, System, Region Where the component is in the inventory and in the machine. Beam Destinations The destinations the component takes part in. Unpowered Whether it is unpowered. Masked Whether it is masked and, if so, when, by whom, the kind of mask, the reason and the expiration. Source Where the component's record comes from: INTERNAL when it was entered in SRM, or a link to the element in the CEBAF, LERF or UITF element database. Added Date When it was added to SRM. History opens its inventory history, for admins.

Admins and the branch's admins also get a Modify link to the component on Setup › Component List.

items.title: Group Responsibility
items.text:
Group Resp. in the menu. Which groups are responsible for which systems: Group, System, Checklist Required, a link to View the checklist, Checklist Published (with who published it and when) and Checklist Modified Date.

Set Checklist Missing to Yes to list the responsibilities that require a checklist and don't have a published one: these are the groups that can't sign off yet. See Required checklists.

items.title: Group Leader
items.text: The leaders of each group, by last name, first name and username. Leaders are the people who can sign off as Ready for the group; they come from the lab's user directory, through the role set for the group on Setup › Group List.

items.title: Signoff Activity
items.text:
The history of signoffs, newest first, one row for each component, group and change: Modified Date, Modified By, Change and Status (such as "Upgrade; Ready"), Component, Group and Comments. It starts with yesterday 7:00 to today 7:00 for the current run's destinations. Beyond the common filters it has User, Status (the status the change set) and Change:

Change Meaning Upgrade The signoff moved toward Ready: Not Ready to Checked, or Checked to Ready. A change to Not Applicable is also an upgrade. Downgrade The signoff moved away from Ready, or out of Not Applicable. Cascade The signoff was lowered because an earlier group downgraded. Comment A comment was added and the status stayed the same.

Masking a component shows here as a Comment on each of its signoffs, with the mask as the status and "Masked" as the comment; unmasking shows as an upgrade or downgrade of each.

The history of a component that has been deleted isn't shown.

items.title: Inventory Activity
items.text:
For admins and branch admins: the record of changes to the inventory. Transactions lists each saved change, newest first, with its ID, date, who made it, from which computer, and the changes in it, such as "MOD Component 0L03" (ADD, MOD or DEL of a Component, System or Category). Select a change to see that item's revisions side by side, oldest first, with every field as it was at each revision.

The Component, System and Category links at the top open the same revision pages by ID. The History link on a component's detail is the easy way in for a component.

Signoffs aren't part of the inventory; their history is in Signoff Activity.

items.title: All Activity
items.text:
One feed, newest first, of signoff changes and inventory changes together. Signoffs made together (the same person, minute, system, group, status and comment) are one entry, with a link such as 12 Components to the individual rows in Signoff Activity.

It has the filters of Signoff Activity, with three kinds of status: Action Status is the status a signoff set, Component Status is the component's status now, and Group Status is the status now of the chosen Group's signoff.

Each entry names its kind of change:

Change Meaning UPGRADE, DOWNGRADE, CASCADE, COMMENT A signoff change, as in Signoff Activity. ADD_COMPONENT, DELETE_COMPONENT, RENAME_COMPONENT A component was added, deleted or renamed. COMPONENT_SYSTEM, MODIFY_REGION A component moved to another system or region. UNPOWER, POWER A component was marked unpowered, or powered again. MASK, UNMASK A component was masked or unmasked; the entry shows the reason. LINK, UNLINK A component was tied to an element database record, or made internal again. ADD_SYSTEM, DELETE_SYSTEM, RENAME_SYSTEM, REORGANIZE_SYSTEM A system was added, deleted, renamed or moved to another category. ADD_CATEGORY, DELETE_CATEGORY, RENAME_CATEGORY, REORGANIZE_CATEGORY A category was added, deleted, renamed or moved.

Changes to systems and categories aren't tied to a component, so most of the filters hide them, including the current run's destinations that the report starts with. Clear the filter to see them.

items.title: Signing off
items.text:
User Guide › Signing off

A signoff is one responsible group's statement about one component: Not Ready, Checked, Ready or Not Applicable. The Signoff tab is where a group works through the components of a system. Anyone can view it; log in to make changes.

items.title: Finding your components
items.text:
The page asks for two things before it lists anything:

  1. Group: the group you are signing off for.
  2. System: the list narrows to the systems that group is responsible for.

Select Apply and the grid shows the system's components that match. To pick the system first, tick Start with Category/System: choose a category (optional) and a system, and the Group list narrows to the groups responsible for it. The All link beside System points to the Readiness tab and the Signoff report, which show every system at once.

Step 3 of the filter is optional and narrows the components:

Filter Keeps components Beam Destination that take part in any of the chosen destinations. Current Run chooses the current run's destinations. Region in any of the chosen regions. Status where the selected group's signoff is one of the chosen statuses. Exclude N/A chooses Ready, Checked and Not Ready. Ready Turn Yes: where it is the selected group's turn. No: where it isn't. Component whose name matches; use % as a wildcard, such as MQB1A%. Min Last Modified, Max Last Modified where the selected group's signoff was last changed in that time range.

The filter is part of the page's address, so a filtered Signoff page can be bookmarked or sent to a colleague.

items.title: The grid
items.text:
Each row is a component, and each column is one of the system's responsible groups, numbered in signoff order. The selected group's column is highlighted; the other columns are there so you can see where the component stands with the groups before and after yours.

  • A cell's icon is that group's status for the component. Hover over it for the comment, who changed it, when, and the kind of change.
  • An icon before a component's name means it is masked, and a ★ after the name means it is unpowered.
  • Select a component's name for its Component Information dialog, or a group's name in the heading for the group's description and leaders.
  • Tick Show Comments to show each signoff's comment in the grid. The icon beside a comment opens that signoff's history.

If the page says a checklist "must be published before signoffs can be made", the group's checklist for this system is required and not published yet; publish it first.

items.title: Changing signoffs
items.text:
1. Select the cells to change, in the selected group's column: select one, hold Ctrl (⌘ on a Mac) to add more, or drag across several. The icon in the column's heading selects the whole column. Unselect All starts over.
  2. Select Edit Signoff. The dialog lists the group and the components.
  3. Choose the Status, and write a Comment saying what you checked or what is wrong.
  4. Select Save. Every selected component gets the same status and comment, at the same time.

You sign off for one group at a time. To leave the status as it is and only add a note, choose the status the signoff already has and write the comment.

items.title: Signoff rules
items.text:
To set You must be And Checked or Not Ready logged in Ready a leader of the group, an admin, or an admin of the component's branch the signoff must be Checked first: Not Ready can't go straight to Ready. Not Applicable a leader of the group, an admin, or an admin of the component's branch at least one other group must have something other than Not Applicable for the component.

SRM doesn't check which group you belong to when you set Checked or Not Ready, so anyone who finds a problem can downgrade a component. Sign off only for your own group otherwise.

SRM also refuses:

  • a signoff on a masked component, whatever the kind of mask. The mask has to be removed first;
  • a signoff for a group whose required checklist isn't published, unless you are an admin;
  • a save that changes nothing: the same status needs a comment.

items.title: Whose turn it is
items.text:
A system's groups sign off in order, each building on the one before: for example the group that installs a device, then the group that powers it, then the group that controls it. It is a group's turn on a component when the groups before it are Ready (or Not Applicable) and its own signoff is still Not Ready or Checked. The Ready Turn filter, here and on the Signoff report, lists those components.

The order is guidance: SRM doesn't stop a group from signing off before its turn.

items.title: Downgrades and cascades
items.text:
Downgrade a signoff, to Checked or Not Ready, whenever the component stops being ready: it broke, it is being worked on, or what you verified no longer holds. Operations relies on this to know the state of the machine from day to day; see the FAQ.

A downgrade can also pull down the groups after yours, since what they verified rested on your signoff. This is a cascade, and Downgrade Options... under the grid sets how far it goes:

Option Choices Default Ready Cascades To nothing, Checked, Not Ready Checked Checked Cascades To nothing, Not Ready nothing

With the defaults, downgrading your signoff turns every later group's Ready into Checked, so those groups look again and confirm, and leaves their Checked signoffs alone. The cascaded signoffs get your comment and show as a Cascade in the activity reports. A downgrade that cascades needs a comment. Groups before yours are never changed.

items.title: Needs Attention
items.text: Tick Needs Attention (Create OPS-PR) to also post an operations problem report to the electronic logbook, with your comment as its text, for a problem that Operations needs to follow up. SRM shows a link to the new entry. Without the tick, the signoff is recorded in SRM only.

items.title: Requesting a mask
items.text: When a component can't be made ready and the program can run without it for now, ask for it to be masked: select its cells, select Request Masking, and give the Reason and the Mask Expiration. See Requesting a mask.

items.title: Other ways to sign off
items.text:
• On the Readiness tab, select a group under a component to change that one signoff.
  • An admin can sign off a whole system at once, or run a saved set of signoffs, from the Setup tab: see Bulk Signoff and Saved Signoffs.
  • Group leaders get a daily email of their group's new outstanding signoffs, when it is turned on, with links to the Signoff tab.
